flawed_step: The first unjustified step is assuming that the graph obtained by contracting the triangle has a 3-edge-colouring. The lifting step is valid if such a colouring exists, but contraction can produce the Petersen graph, which is not 3-edge-colourable.
counterexample: Let the Petersen graph have vertices u0,...,u4,v0,...,v4 and edges ui-u(i+1), ui-vi, and vi-v(i+2), with indices modulo 5. Replace u0 by a triangle a,b,c, attaching a-u1, b-u4, and c-v0. Explicitly, the resulting graph G has vertices {a,b,c,u1,u2,u3,u4,v0,v1,v2,v3,v4} and edges {ab,bc,ca,a-u1,b-u4,c-v0,u1-u2,u2-u3,u3-u4,u1-v1,u2-v2,u3-v3,u4-v4,v0-v2,v2-v4,v4-v1,v1-v3,v3-v0}. Every listed vertex has degree 3, and G is finite and simple. It is bridgeless: every Petersen edge lies on a cycle, and replacing each passage through u0 by a path through the triangle preserves such cycles; each new triangle edge also lies on a cycle because the Petersen graph with u0 removed is connected. Suppose G had a 3-edge-colouring. The three triangle edges, being pairwise adjacent, would receive all three colours. Consequently a-u1, b-u4, and c-v0 would receive the respective missing colours and hence would be pairwise differently coloured. Contracting {a,b,c} would therefore give a 3-edge-colouring of the Petersen graph. This is impossible. Indeed, in a cubic 3-edge-colouring each colour class is a perfect matching M, while the complement of M must be a union of even cycles alternating the other two colours. For a Petersen perfect matching, the number of spokes ui-vi is odd. Three spokes are impossible because the two remaining outer indices would need to differ by 1 modulo 5 while the same two inner indices would need to differ by 2. With five spokes, the complement is the two 5-cycles. With one spoke, rotational symmetry reduces to u0-v0; the forced matching is {u0-v0,u1-u2,u3-u4,v2-v4,v1-v3}, whose complement is the two 5-cycles (u0,u1,v1,v4,u4) and (v0,v2,u2,u3,v3). Thus every possible complement contains odd cycles, proving that the Petersen graph, and hence G, is not 3-edge-colourable.
assessment_summary: The lifting observation is correct: a colouring of the contracted graph extends uniquely across the triangle. It does not establish that the contracted graph is colourable. Expanding a vertex of the Petersen graph into a triangle gives an explicit simple, bridgeless cubic graph containing a triangle but having no 3-edge-colouring.
